company_description:
A century ago, James Mitchell – engineer, builder, entrepreneur, and man of the world – traveled to the American South and made the first big bet for Southern Company.  Mitchell was so inspired by the hydro potential of Alabama’s rivers that he dreamed of developing a series of dams to electrify the Southeast.  To bring his dream to life, he sketched out a regional power network, raised money from British investors, and created the first of the three forerunner holding companies that would play prominent roles in Southern Company’s history.

In the century since, Southern Company and its predecessor companies have faced every conceivable impediment to progress – natural and man-made disasters, a hostile takeover, financial challenges and numerous threats and attempts to pull its business apart and scramble the pieces.  Rather than being destroyed by these challenges, Southern Company grew stronger, more resilient, and more committed to its mission.  That Southern Company has not only survived for a century but also empowered the South to thrive is a reflection on the leaders who emerged to shepherd the company safely into tomorrow.

Through expansions, customer growth, mergers, acquisitions and divestitures, today Southern Company is a leading energy company serving 9 million customers through its subsidiaries. The company provides clean, safe, reliable and affordable energy through electric operating companies in three states, natural gas distribution companies in four states, a competitive generation company serving wholesale customers across America, a leading distributed energy infrastructure company, a fiber optics network and telecommunications services. Southern Company brands are known for excellent customer service, high reliability and affordable prices below the national average.

GovCIO was founded by a Navy veteran and a government consultant who saw a need for fresh ideas in the government IT space and had the desire to make an impact.

Sitting at a kitchen table, they built GovCIO. Together, they created a unique organization that combines extensive Federal experience and innovative and disruptive approaches with a caring, inclusive culture that puts customers before profit.

While our leadership has changed, we’re 1,000 times bigger – with well over 2,000 employees.

And while we definitely don’t fit at a kitchen table anymore (or at any of our first three downtown D.C. offices for that matter), the core of what makes us who we are still remains.

Great People Do Great Things

It’s simple— great people do great things— for our customers, our culture, and our ability to attract other great people.

Our Pursuit of Workplace Happiness

We spend a lot of time at work, and it’s a lot more gratifying when you’re comfortable being yourself, able to treat co-workers like friends, and you actually want to be there.

GovCIO is filled with amazing people who are silly, passionate, joyful, and funny; and we’ve worked hard to cultivate a culture that allows our amazing people to do amazing work.

Regardless of whether you work in our offices or remotely, we strive to foster a fun, welcoming, and empowering work environment that makes you want to go to work each day.

And when you’re happy at work, you do your best work, which is a win for everyone- you, us, and our customers.

title: Technical Support Specialist 3 -4P/912
description:
**Title:** **Technical Support Specialist III – Energy Management Systems** 
**Client:** **Southern Company Services** 
**Location:** **Birmingham, AL** 
**Contract:** **2 Years** 
**Schedule:** **24x7x365 rotating shift environment** 
**Shift Length:** **8- or 12-hour shifts, including nights, weekends, and holidays**


**Job Summary**
---------------

We are seeking a **Technical Support Specialist III – Energy Management Systems (EMS)** to provide frontline technical support for critical SCADA and Energy Management Systems.

This position is part of a contracted **24x7x365 operations team** responsible for system monitoring, diagnostics, incident response, application support, customer communication, and coordination with technical support personnel and management.

The ideal candidate will have experience supporting critical IT or operational systems and be comfortable working in a high-availability, regulated environment.

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

* Monitor primary **SCADA and ancillary EMS systems** for health, performance, and availability.
* Provide frontline diagnostics and problem resolution for EMS applications and computer systems.
* Coordinate repair and troubleshooting activities with EMS personnel and other technical support groups.
* Notify key customers regarding system outages, incidents, and events affecting critical systems.
* Track and document incidents and support cases through completion.
* Follow established knowledge-based troubleshooting procedures.
* Adhere to formal Change Management processes.
* Support Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery systems.
* Maintain compliance with electronic and physical access requirements.
* Communicate operational issues clearly to customers, technical teams, coordinators, and management.
* Prioritize incidents based on criticality and potential impact to the Bulk Power System.
* Provide feedback regarding process improvements and recurring customer issues.
* Maintain strong working relationships with transmission control center personnel and other key customers.

**Required Qualifications**
---------------------------

* Formal education in **Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field** , or equivalent professional experience.
* Experience supporting computer systems, applications, or technical operations.
* Strong troubleshooting and critical-thinking skills.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
* Strong customer-service skills.
* Ability to work effectively in a team-oriented and potentially high-stress environment.
* Ability to multitask and prioritize incidents based on operational impact.
* Ability to follow documented procedures and Change Management processes.
* Ability to work rotating shifts, including:

  + Days
  + Nights
  + Weekends
  + Holidays

**Technical Knowledge**
-----------------------

Working knowledge or experience with the following is preferred:

* Windows operating systems
* AIX
* UNIX-based operating systems
* Distributed computer networks
* SCADA systems
* Energy Management Systems
* Business Continuity systems
* Disaster Recovery environments
* Incident and case-management processes

**Compliance Requirements**
---------------------------

Candidates must be able to comply with applicable regulatory and security requirements, including:

* Critical Infrastructure Protection (CIP)
* Sarbanes-Oxley requirements
* Federal regulatory compliance requirements
* Electronic and physical access policies
* Federal Energy Regulatory Commission Standards of Conduct
* Southern Company Separation Protocol
* Southern Company Insider Threat Program requirements

Enhanced background screening and drug screening may be required.

**Work Requirements**
---------------------

* This position operates in a **24x7x365 environment** .
* Shifts may be 8 or 12 hours.
* Schedule rotates between day and night shifts.
* Weekend and holiday coverage is required.
* During severe weather events, personnel may be required to remain local to or sequestered near the control center.

**Key Skills**
--------------

**Energy Management Systems | EMS | SCADA | Technical Support | Application Support | Windows | UNIX | AIX | Incident Management | Change Management | CIP Compliance | Disaster Recovery | Business Continuity | Critical Infrastructure | 24x7 Operations | Bulk Power System**
